source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade / Downgrade BIOS firmware by Redfish when system is off
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade BIOS firmware through redfish.
1. Enter the command on the command line to set the behavior of BMC after update.
Command : curl -k -X PATCH https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/ -H "Content-Type:application/json" -d '{"HttpPushUriOptions":{"HttpPushUriApplyTime":{"ApplyTime": "Immediate"}}}'
2. Change the name of the firmware file to be updated in the green text. This command may take some time to upload the firmware to BMC.
Command : curl -k -X POST https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update -H "Content-Type:application/octet-stream" --data-binary @${File_name}
3. Waiting for the flash progress complete.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Firmware should be flashed successfully.
curl -k -X GET https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl (Redfish REST client, on the BMC side) + BIOS image (user provides)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- BIOS downgrade via Redfish (system is off): the agent needs the exact user-provided BIOS image first the host must be powered OFF first (flash while system is off), then runs the Redfish update flow: `PATCH /redfish/v1/UpdateService` (set preserve/replace behavior), `POST /redfish/v1/UpdateService` to upload the image, poll the returned TaskService task to completion, then `GET /redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory` to confirm the new version is active. Not a single one-liner; run step-by-step after the image is placed on the BMC.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the full Redfish PATCH/POST response, the TaskService poll loop, and the final `FirmwareInventory` JSON so the user confirms the BIOS version changed and the SUT powers on cleanly after the off-state flash.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: BIOS firmware flash via Redfish is state-changing and can brick the BMC/host if interrupted; flash only the user-specified image with host powered off for a clean result, and never interrupt mid-flash.

original_test_intent: Automatically upgrade and downgrade BIOS through Redfish with the host off, then verify the intended BIOS is active and the server completes the required POST/boot and configuration checks.
original_method: Verify host-off/BMC-on state, configure update apply behavior, POST a selected BIOS image, wait for completion, query FirmwareInventory and inspect logs before bringing the host through the approved activation/boot sequence.
manual_activity: An authorized engineer supplies/approves the immutable BIOS, region and activation plan and later issues the verdict; the core Redfish, host-state, task, power-control and evidence flow is software-automatable where approved interfaces exist.
required_inputs: Board/current/upgrade/downgrade BIOS versions, signed image hashes and region policy
Required BIOS settings, POST/OS and health expectations
Protected credentials, trusted CA, flashback/recovery and stable standby power
safety_requirements: Reject embedded credentials and `curl -k`; authenticate through protected secrets and trusted endpoint identity.
Verify exact board and BIOS region compatibility; do not infer from filename or generic FirmwareInventory.
Do not assume Immediate apply or `/update`; discover the vendor action and correlate its task.
Never retry, reverse or power-cycle after an uncertain task; preserve Redfish, console and SEL failure evidence.
agent_execution_scope: After approval, verify host-off/BMC-on state, image/region identity and capability; execute one transition, monitor the advertised task/activation, then collect BIOS inventory/settings, console POST, OS/kernel, BMC and SEL evidence.
Report execution status/tool result separately; do not assign PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve BIOS images/regions, version order, activation sequence, settings contract and recovery.
Evaluate boot/configuration evidence and issue separate verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The general Redfish lifecycle matches, but original URL credentials, TLS bypass and assumed endpoint are unsafe. Image/approval requirements do not reduce automatable capability.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a vendor-approved capability-discovered Redfish BIOS update action with trusted TLS, protected credentials, response-correlated task handling and project-approved activation/host-power control.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The host-off condition, source PATCH/POST/GET, script and 10/30-minute values remain; no unsupported reset count is added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind a signed image and region policy to the exact board, discover the advertised BIOS update action, submit one approved transition, monitor the correlated task and activation sequence, and independently validate active BIOS, settings, console POST, OS/kernel, BMC and SEL health.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: BMC/BIOS combinations exposing a vendor-approved Redfish BIOS update path while the host is off.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record Redfish schema/service, board/BIOS/BMC/image/client/CA and recovery-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor BIOS-over-Redfish update, apply-time, region-preservation, activation and recovery documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces embedded secrets and assumed URI with discovered secure action; adds region, activation, settings, POST and recovery evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Preserves both transition directions and detects nonbootable or misconfigured firmware despite an API success response.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: FirmwareInventory alone may not prove boot-block or settings behavior; independent console and boot evidence remain required.

project_override_considerations: A project may define images, regions, activation timing and automated host-power method. Completion claims only that exact plan, version pair and settings contract.
expected_evidence: Approved platform/BIOS/region transition matrix and hashes
Host-off/BMC-standby baseline and advertised action discovery
Redacted update response, correlated task and activation/power timeline
Pre/post active BIOS inventory and required settings
Console POST, OS/kernel, BMC/SEL health and recovery readiness
Tool result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source coherently targets BIOS via Redfish with the host off and does not prescribe contradictory reset semantics. Image, region, action and acceptance details are identifiable project inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Unsafe literal commands are preserved but need not be executed; a secure vendor capability flow can implement the same function. Missing project artifacts affect readiness, not capability or intent.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes PARTIAL to FULLY AUTOMATABLE while retaining host-off and BIOS scope and correcting unsafe assumptions.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps its security, POST and recovery gates but changes BLOCKED because the exact vendor contract can be supplied without redefining the test.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Cleanly separates software capability, approved destructive readiness, tool result and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Adds BIOS-region and boot/configuration evidence to an automatable, response-correlated Redfish state machine.
independent_technical_reasoning: The core workflow is an API operation plus programmable host power and observable software/console evidence. With a fixed approved plan, every core step can be automated; firmware risk requires approval and recovery but not a lower automation class.
